coordinates.note: Given to the arcminute (35 deg 47' N, 138 deg 30' E); the 100 km2 array is spread around the observatory, so 3 km is only the uncertainty of this point, not the extent of the array. The ICRR observatory page prints the same coordinates in Japanese.
coordinates.quote: We constructed a very large surface array at the Akeno Observatory (35o 47' N, 138o 30' E)

summary.plain: The mountain research station in Yamanashi, Japan, where the 100-square-kilometre AGASA array of particle detectors recorded giant cosmic-ray air showers from 1990 to 2004.
summary.technical: Akeno Observatory of the University of Tokyo's Institute for Cosmic Ray Research, Akeno-cho, Hokuto, Yamanashi, at 35 deg 47' N, 138 deg 30' E and 900 m; centre of the AGASA surface array.
